retention_notes: All 568 process samples and every measured/warmup timing from four timing campaigns are retained as numeric samples; no outliers removed.
Repeated source manifests, output witnesses and command arrays are interned by content hash. Each raw stdout has a SHA-256; timing lines are represented by the retained arrays.
Timing medians are per-process medians followed by the median across processes. Initial-candidate evidence is retained separately and not attributed to the final code.

wait4 RSS includes the whole child lifetime and may inherit a pre-exec launch floor. The repeated approximately 47 MiB native/CPython values resolve no heap difference. Independent GNU time native measurements supersede those values for native peak RSS.
Callgrind attribution is inclusive and non-additive; counts cover the whole process including the initial correctness repair plus one timed repair.
GC collection/heap statistics are neither allocation counts nor final retained-memory measurements. Native total allocation/copy bytes and post-repair retained heap were not instrumented.

tracemalloc_reproduction.source:
import gc,json,sys,tracemalloc
from json_repair import repair_json
for n in (2000,4000,8000):
 source='{"a":"'+'x\\n'*n+'end",}'
 expected={'a':'x\n'*n+'end'}
 rows=[]
 for sample in range(5):
  gc.collect()
  tracemalloc.start()
  result=repair_json(source,return_objects=True)
  assert result==expected
  gc.collect()
  retained,peak=tracemalloc.get_traced_memory()
  tracemalloc.stop()
  rows.append({'retained_with_result_bytes':retained,'peak_traced_bytes':peak})
 print(json.dumps({'engine':sys.version,'fragments':n,'samples':rows}))
tracemalloc_reproduction.note: Use this exact source in a separate process for each variant; the source/expected payloads precede tracing, and the repaired result stays retained through gc.collect().
